_comment: The single source for every number shown to a reader. docs/documentation-plan.md §3: figures render from an artifact, never from typed prose, and each carries the date and sample size it was measured with. docs/measurements.md is the narrative version of this file; the in-app 'How it works' panels read this one. Regenerate from arena/ladder.py and bench/benchmark.py rather than editing by hand.
conditions: EVAL rules (Weis, Stöck and the match bonus off), double rounds, paired t-test, agents bidding for trump

ladder.note: Rule-based trump selection for all agents, so these compare card play only.

trump_selection.note: Identical card play on both sides; only the bidding differs.

conventions.note: Table conventions on against off, identical search budget both sides. They only re-order moves the search rated the same, so what is being tested is that they cost nothing — not that they gain.

signal_reading.note: Reading the discard convention into the determinization prior. Two nulls and one borderline p=0.049 that did not replicate; reported as a null and off by default. See measurements.md §5c.

game_objective.note: Projecting the round onto the game instead of maximising the round's share. Whole games, paired, HOUSE rules — arena/games.py, because the round-level instrument cannot see this and would score it backwards. Three versions; the first two lost, the third is harmless. See measurements.md §5d.

bidding_prior.note: Reading the bidding into the imagined hands — the strongest prior available, and null. measurements.md §5e has the mechanism: a prior only flips decisions the search already rates within 0.008 of each other.

adversarial_search.note: Modelling the other team as opponents. The tree maximised the root team's value at every node, including theirs, so it valued lines by what happens when the opposition cooperates. A correctness fix; pooled +0.30% +/- 0.32 over n=1800, never significant.

split_sweep.note: How a fixed budget is split between determinizations and iterations, endgame solver off. An inverted U with a broad flat top: at least ~10 worlds and ~30 iterations each, and within that nothing matters. Closes the 'allocation guidance' explanation in measurements.md §3.

risk_aversion.note: Concave kink in the reward to offset determinized search's optimism. All null, drifting slightly negative. An affine penalty would have been provably a no-op; see measurements.md §5f.

leaf_evaluator.note: Phase 0 of value-net-plan.md: a linear evaluator fitted to the random playout's own mean. Nine points worse at every split. The playout's error is zero-mean and washes out across 2400 samples to ~0.019; the evaluator's is bias at 0.232 and never washes out. Kill criterion fired. See measurements.md §5g.

ismcts.note: Information Set MCTS: one tree shared across every imagined world instead of a tree per world and a vote. The first change in this file to make the bot stronger. Replicated three times. See measurements.md §5h.

resample_every.note: Iterations sharing one imagined world. The gain is intact at 4 and gone at 8 — a cliff, not a slope. Shipped default 4: full advantage at 1.41x the determinized search rather than 1.95x.

fusion.note: The gap to a bot that sees all four hands, endgame solver off. It narrows by 0.74 of ~9 points, so strategy fusion is real and is about 8% of what hidden information costs.

policy_prior.note: Hand-written best-play knowledge in the selection rule rather than the reward, so it steers the search without biasing the value. Ordering null; the PUCT hump at c=1 was the best of five comparisons and did not replicate; c=4 is significantly worse, which proves the prior is active and wrong. Same lesson as greedy==random. See measurements.md §5i.

learned_prior.note: A policy distilled from 40,190 of the search's own decisions, in the same slot as the hand-written prior of §5i. 48% top-1 agreement, and it recovers the Swiss conventions from self-play — but null in play, did not replicate, and a uniform-prior control is null too. Structural reason: 4.2 legal moves and 2,400 iterations means ~571 visits per candidate, so there is nothing for a prior to prune. See measurements.md §5j.

budget_sweep.note: Each budget played against a fixed 2,400-iteration reference, endgame solver off.

throughput.note: Search budget 2,400 iterations — the measured saturation point.

endgame.note: Exact double-dummy solve, median nodes visited. Roughly 15x per extra card, which is why the solver replaces the search rather than running at every leaf.

literature.human_parity: 49.5% ± 14.2% of points, six experienced human teams over 136 rounds, against a DMCTS team
literature.trump_selection_claim: ~16 points of win rate over choosing at random
